title: GraphQL variable definitions, references and selected fields named like credentials, with no value
summary: Synthetic GraphQL requests and error responses in which names such as $apiKey, apiKey and token appear only as a variable definition, a variable use, a member name or a selected field, with no value supplied.
rationale: In GraphQL a name is not a value: a variable definition names a variable and its type, a variable use refers to it, and a selected field such as token asks for a value without containing one. A document can therefore be full of credential-like names and hold no secret bytes, for example when the variables member is absent, or the response says only which variable was invalid. The failure mode is a name-driven false alarm; the same field may carry a secret in a response, which is a separate input with a value in it. Whether a named variable that does have a value is secret is the value-side question of the other cases and is not decided from the name.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged: the inputs contain no value bytes for the named variables. This follows from the cited specification text on variable definitions and values supplied separately, and from the response format, whose message is developer text; it makes no claim about any value that might be supplied under the same names. Project-authored, not independent.

sources.supports: A variable is defined at the top of the operation with a name and a type, and its value is provided as part of the request, separately.
An operation selects the set of information it needs by listing fields by name in a selection set (Example 7: id, firstName, lastName) and receives that information in the response.
The variables parameter is optional; null or absent is equivalent.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Research for #197 (parent #158). Origin of the inputs: evidence-derived and synthetic, not observed in a real incident or product; the request shapes follow the specification examples and the response texts are invented. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. The twin with a supplied value is graphql-variables-map-value-and-literal-beside-variable-references. Placeholders, masks and documentation values in the same positions are covered by existing cases.
